difficulty.label: basic_learning
difficulty.rationale: Single-concept item: interpret a two-row concordance table and select the conclusion it supports (genetic contribution to risk, not determinism). Distractors are clearly flawed (overstated determinism, claiming no environmental influence, reversed inference), so the item has one defensible answer. No calculation is needed and reading is minimal.

difficulty.label: exam_prep
difficulty.rationale: Single named concept (diathesis-stress) applied to a small two-row table. Students must read the concordance data, recall that identical twins share all their genes, and reason that a rate well below 100% implies environmental/stress contributions. Distractors are clearly wrong (stress alone, misdiagnosis, half-genes error), so there is no ambiguity. Moderate reasoning with a table-to-concept representation change fits a standard mock-exam item, on the easier end.

difficulty.label: exam_prep
difficulty.rationale: Student must read a simple two-row table, recognize the twin-study (behavioral genetics) design, and reason about how to separate genetic from shared-environment effects. The correct option (identical twins reared apart vs. together) requires understanding the logic of controlling genes while varying environment, and distractors are clearly weaker. This is a typical AP multiple-choice research-design/application item, with no heavy computation or reading and no ambiguity. Minor note: the stem asks for the best follow-up study rather than directly asking for the design type, so skill alignment with 2.A is slightly loose.
